encoded_source_commitments.text: Decision validity and authorization validity remain separate.
A still-reasonable decision does not automatically preserve execution permission.

primary_runs.rationale: JANUS separates decision, authorization, and execution. The Orientation Edition describes authorization as a separate fact with its own owner, history, and conditions, and describes fail-closed behavior when a required condition is not met. The document supports blocking silent execution; the harness uses 'reauthorize' as its own disposition shorthand for obtaining a new valid authorization state if execution is still desired.
source_basis: §01 Protective Principle — decision, authorization, and execution are separate concepts.
§19 Operational Control — authorization is a separate fact with its own owner, history, and conditions.
§32 Security by Design — when a condition is not met, prefer no transition over a silent bypass.
primary_runs.open_question: What exact event invalidates A1, and what JANUS mechanism determines whether a new authorization fact is required?
primary_runs.evidence_required: A reconstructable record of E1, D1, A1, the C1→C2 change, the authority owner, the decision to stop or continue, and any subsequent authorization event.

encoded_source_commitments.text: The no-forced-resolution principle for conflicting data is applied here to conflicting decision evidence.
Authorization history and current epistemic justification are different facts.
The dependency rule linking evidence invalidation to authority invalidation is not stated.

primary_runs.rationale: JANUS distinguishes evidence, decision, authorization, and execution, and treats contradiction as information that must remain visible. Blocking execution on a materially changed evidentiary basis is a reasonable orientation-level inference. Whether authorization is automatically suspended, separately revoked, or later reissued is not stated.
source_basis: §06 Distinctions — evidence, decision, authorization, and execution are distinct classes.
§28 Conflict — data conflict should remain explicit rather than be forced into a single value.
§29 Resilience and §38 Working Contract — unjustified transitions should not gain more power than their grounding supports.

encoded_source_commitments.text: Historical authorization can remain true as history while no longer proving present authority under a stipulated bound.
The document's scope-of-validity language is explicit for memory and is applied here by analogy to authorization validity.
No authorization TTL, expiry object, or renewal mechanism is specified.

primary_runs.rationale: The Orientation Edition does not define authorization expiry, but this scenario stipulates a validity bound. Given that stipulation, JANUS's separation of current state, historical state, authorization conditions, and fail-closed behavior supports blocking execution after the bound has lapsed. 'Reauthorize' is harness shorthand, not a JANUS term.

§39 Limits — conditions can change and trust must have context; §32 supplies the fail-closed principle.

encoded_source_commitments.text: Learning can change knowledge or preference without changing authorization.
Capability expansion is not authority expansion.
The exact verification evidence and governance event required for expanded authority are not specified.

primary_runs.rationale: JANUS directly states that learning must not become self-promotion and that a new ability should not automatically receive a new level of authority. The headline disposition applies to the attempted expansion beyond S1, not to already authorized in-scope work.
source_basis: §22 Learning from Experience — Learning ≠ Self-Promotion.
§24 Maturity — capability development and authority development remain separate; governance decides whether change is accepted.
§38 Working Contract — an improved model is not, by itself, consent to greater power.

encoded_source_commitments.text: The no-forced-resolution principle stated for data conflict is applied here to authority conflict.
Fail-closed / refusal-of-unjustified-transition principles do not support silent execution on an unresolved basis.
The authority-resolution hierarchy itself is not specified.

primary_runs.rationale: JANUS does not define an organizational authority lattice, policy-precedence system, or jurisdiction hierarchy. Therefore the mechanism for resolving O1 versus O2 is unspecified. Separately, its fail-closed and refusal-of-unjustified-transition principles weigh against silently executing on one side of an unresolved authority conflict. Applying §28's data-conflict language to authority conflict is explicitly marked as an analogy rather than direct support.

primary_runs.changed: The authority state changes while a previously authorized action is already affecting the external environment.
primary_runs.remains_valid: The record that X1 began under valid authorization remains part of the historical evidence.
primary_runs.invalid_or_uncertain: The assumption that the Orientation Edition determines one universal response for every in-flight action.
primary_runs.execution: The Orientation Edition establishes an accountable execution boundary but does not specify whether an in-flight action must stop, safely complete, roll back, compensate, or escalate.

encoded_source_commitments.text: Execution remains separately accountable from the authorization that preceded it.
The authority-loss event should be reconstructable as part of the audit trail even though 'revocation' is not a named JANUS event.
No universal in-flight authority-loss mechanism is specified at orientation level.

primary_runs.rationale: JANUS treats execution as a distinct accountable event and requires enough trace to reconstruct authority and outcome. The Orientation Edition intentionally remains above implementation specification and does not define universal semantics for authority loss during execution. The harness therefore refuses to invent one.
source_basis: §20 Execution — execution is an accountable boundary event.

primary_runs.evidence_required: The authorization state at execution start, the revocation or condition-change event, action interruptibility/reversibility characteristics, the response selected, and the resulting external effect.

determinism.method: Per scenario: 3 runs with Reset between, then 1 run after full page reload. Compared disposition, badge, rationale, commitments, cards/sources/question/evidence, event log, pre-replay record, replay record, export key set, export body excluding generated_at, contract hash, source hash (SHA-256 prefixes).
determinism.note: Event-log hashes equal the corresponding matrix-run hashes (M01, M08, M16, M21, M30, M35). generated_at and filename timestamp differ by design. The authorization-expiry export-body prefix was redacted by the browser tool's output filter; its identity check (true) was computed in-page.

DEF-02.evidence: Wording now 're-derivation from the static authored scenario contract'; contract-hash tamper (T4, T8, T9) and disposition tamper (T1, T2) produce DIVERGENCE; 36/36 + repeat normal replays CONSISTENT.
DEF-02.remaining_concern: Source-document hash check is tautological (NEW-02, T7, T12); replay does not cover prediction/comparison/text fields (T3, T5, T6).

DEF-03.evidence: Export has generated_at, version, build_id, source URL+SHA, contract SHA, summary, perturbation, event log, replay, attributions, restrictions, evidence_required; filenames unique; the two recommended assertions refuse T1, T3, T10.
DEF-03.remaining_concern: No harness commit SHA; source URL relative; source SHA is a constant; export proceeds after replay divergence and on consistently-tampered records (NEW-03); generated_at is run time.

DEF-04.evidence: Glossary of all six labels in UI and README; three-tier EXACT/PARTIAL/DIFFERENT; S04 execution card: 'Continue only within the already authorized scope. Block the out-of-scope use…'; S02 BLOCK_REAUTHORIZE and ESCALATE now PARTIAL.
DEF-04.remaining_concern: Compatibility sets are undisclosed and uneven (NEW-05).

DEF-06.remaining_concern: Residual: hero 'It evaluates authored architectural interpretations', export 'evaluation_mode'; the replay source-hash and 'internal consistency checks' claims are covered by NEW-02/NEW-03.

DEF-12.evidence: Injected and non-existent values both produce an explicit refusal, Run/Replay/Export disabled, no exception.

NEW-01.title: Async race: selector change/Reset during an in-flight Run leaves stale, exportable evidence
NEW-01.reproduction: From script: runBtn.click(); then, in the same task, change #scenarioSelect (dispatch change) or click Reset.
NEW-01.expected: The later selector change/Reset wins; no result or evidence action survives.
NEW-01.actual: runChallenge() awaits buildEvidence() and then unconditionally writes lastRun and the DOM for the captured scenario/prediction. The S01 result shows under the S06 selector and Export produces a condition-change file. The replay equivalent throws an unhandled TypeError.
NEW-01.impact: Not reachable by normal human interaction (the digest resolves in well under a millisecond), but it breaks the guarantee that evidence can never be exported under mismatched selectors.
NEW-01.recommended_correction: Take a run token/generation counter; after each await, discard the result if the selectors or token changed; null-check lastRun after awaits in replayLastRun().

NEW-02.title: Source-document SHA-256 'check' is tautological and never computed from the document
NEW-02.reproduction: Run → set lastRun.source_document.sha256 = 'fff…' → Replay; or change SOURCE_DOCUMENT.sha256 before Run → Run → Replay → Export.
NEW-02.expected: The replay/export source check compares the recorded hash to a hash computed from the served .docx bytes, so it could diverge.
NEW-02.actual: sourceMatch compares SOURCE_DOCUMENT.sha256 with lastRun.source_document.sha256, which is the same object reference, so it is always true. The .docx is never fetched or hashed. T7: CONSISTENT; T12: exported a wrong hash with source_match=true.
NEW-02.evidence: T7, T12; app.js buildEvidence() 'source_document: SOURCE_DOCUMENT' and replayLastRun() sourceMatch.
NEW-02.impact: The UI/README claim that replay 'compares … source-document SHA-256' implies a verification that cannot fail. This is the same class of overstatement as v0.1 DEF-02/DEF-06.
NEW-02.recommended_correction: Either fetch and hash the .docx (crypto.subtle) at Run and Replay and record computed vs expected, or reword to 'records the published hash (not recomputed)'. Deep-copy SOURCE_DOCUMENT into lastRun.

NEW-03.title: Export 'internal consistency checks' are shallow; divergent or tampered evidence exports
NEW-03.reproduction: T2, T4, T5, T6, T8, T9 (in-memory tamper of lastRun or the contract), then Export.
NEW-03.expected: Export refuses, or clearly flags, records whose disposition, prediction, text or contract hash disagree with the contract or event log, and records whose replay diverged.
NEW-03.actual: Only two checks exist (label vs disposition, comparison vs current contract). Records with a replay DIVERGENCE export normally. A consistently tampered disposition exports alongside the original contract hash with 'NOT PERFORMED BEFORE EXPORT'. The T6 file's name and fields say block_reauthorize/EXACT while its own event_log says BLOCK.
NEW-03.evidence: Tamper table T2, T4, T5, T6, T8, T9.
NEW-03.impact: Requires in-page tampering, and JSON exports are editable after download anyway. However, README's claim 'Export performs internal consistency checks' reads stronger than the implementation.
NEW-03.recommended_correction: At export, recompute the contract hash and compare it with the record; compare event_log lines 2/5/11/14 with the record; refuse export (or set an integrity:'FAILED' field) when replay diverged; reword README to list exactly what is checked.

NEW-04.title: Prediction validation accepts Object prototype keys
NEW-04.reproduction: Inject <option value='constructor'> (or 'toString', '__proto__') into #predictionSelect, select it, click Run, then Export.
NEW-04.actual: labels[prediction] resolves through the prototype chain, so the run proceeds. EVENT 002 shows 'function Object() { [native code] }' / '[object Object]'; the export omits reviewer_prediction_label.
NEW-04.impact: DOM injection only; malformed evidence records.
NEW-04.recommended_correction: Use Object.hasOwn(labels, prediction) or a Set of allowed values, or make labels a null-prototype object.

NEW-05.title: Comparison compatibility sets are authored, undisclosed and uneven
NEW-05.reproduction: Run S06 with CONTINUE; S04 with ESCALATE; S01/S03 with ESCALATE; S05 with BLOCK_REAUTHORIZE.
NEW-05.expected: PARTIAL/DIFFERENT follows a published rule that is consistent with each scenario's own execution card.
NEW-05.actual: S06 CONTINUE = DIFFERENT, yet the S06 card lists 'safely complete' as an outcome the source leaves open (BLOCK and ROLLBACK are PARTIAL). S04 ESCALATE = DIFFERENT, although §24 says 'the governance process decides'. S01/S03 ESCALATE = DIFFERENT, although the S01 card requires 'reevaluation under the applicable governance process'. compatiblePredictions do not appear in the UI, README or export (only inside the contract hash).
NEW-05.evidence: Matrix M04, M16, M22, M27, M31; app.js compatiblePredictions.
NEW-05.impact: Comparison labels can still reflect the author's labelling convention rather than source content (a residual of DEF-04).
NEW-05.recommended_correction: Publish each scenario's compatibility set and a one-line reason; add CONTINUE to S06 (or explain why safe completion ≠ CONTINUE); consider ESCALATE as PARTIAL for S01/S03/S04; export compatible_predictions.

NEW-06.title: Support-status vocabulary undefined and inconsistently applied
NEW-06.reproduction: Read the UI glossary and README; view S02/S03/S05/S06 commitments.
NEW-06.expected: SUPPORTED / REASONABLE INFERENCE / EXTENDED / OPEN defined, visually distinct, and applied at the strength the source supports.
NEW-06.actual: No definitions anywhere. REASONABLE INFERENCE uses the 'extended' CSS class (same colour as analogy). The requested 'DIRECTLY SUPPORTED' distinction is shown as bare 'SUPPORTED'. S03#2 cites memory scope-of-validity (§26), but §26 is absent from S03's source list.
NEW-06.evidence: Screenshot of S06 commitments; app.js renderCommitments(); S03 sources.
NEW-06.impact: Readers cannot tell how strong 'SUPPORTED' is meant to be.
NEW-06.recommended_correction: Add a status glossary; give REASONABLE INFERENCE its own style; rename SUPPORTED → DIRECTLY SUPPORTED where a quote exists; add §26 to S03 sources.

NEW-07.title: Minor state and message polish
NEW-07.actual: (a) The first scenario change on a fresh page says 'Previous result, replay, and export state were invalidated' when none existed. (b) Export after a removed contract (T11) silently does nothing. (c) Hidden result DOM keeps previous values (not visible). (d) generated_at is Run time, while the filename timestamp is Export time.
NEW-07.recommended_correction: Conditional stale message; alert on refused export; clear the result DOM on invalidation; add exported_at.
